findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — P1 (confidence 100): `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` makes a cached denial for the valid `(name="a_b", parent="c")` request collide with `(name="a", parent="b_c")`, so the second request is returned denied without evaluating its distinct resource/folder permissions (the strongest rebuttal is the 30-second TTL and rare identifier pair, which fails because both underscore-bearing UIDs are accepted and a cache key must preserve authorization request identity).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — P1, confidence 100: `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` gives the denied checks `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` the same key, so denial of the first forces an incorrect cached denial of the second for 30 seconds.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — P1, confidence 100: after `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` at line 154 records a denied check, `if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(ctx, permDenialKey); ok { return &authzv1.CheckResponse{Allowed: false}, nil }` returns false for the 30-second TTL without reloading permissions, so a permission grant or folder move immediately after the denial is invisibly rejected even though the positive-cache path falls back to the database when its cached scope does not allow the request.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — P2, confidence 100: `Review the change.` supplies no requirement for which AuthZ path or cache behavior must improve, so the new Check/List/denial-cache policy is not traceable to any stated acceptance criterion; trigger: a regression or alternative design cannot be judged against task scope; rebuttal: the title says `improve authz caching`; fails because it does not delimit client versus server caching, positive versus negative caching, or the requested behavior.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — P3 (confidence 75): `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` concatenates unescaped request-controlled name and parent, so a denied check for `name="foo_bar", parent="baz"` poisons the identical denial key for an allowed `name="foo", parent="bar_baz"` check and forces an authorization denial for 30 seconds.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — [P2, confidence 100] The only denial-cache test injects `s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)` rather than producing a denied `Check`, so deleting the new production write `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` at pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 leaves every test green and the denial cache is never populated.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:905 — [P2, confidence 100] Every added cache-hit test uses `Subject: "user:test-uid"`; deleting `if cached, ok := s.permCache.Get(ctx, anonPermKey); ok { return cached, nil }` at pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:349 leaves every test green, so anonymous cached `Check` and `List` calls can regress to backend reads undetected.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:979 — [P2, confidence 100] The denial test seeds its sentinel through the mirrored helper `userPermDenialCacheKey(...)` and uses one resource only, so deleting `name + "_" + parent` from pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 leaves every test green while a denial for dash1/fold1 also denies dash2/fold2.

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — P1, confidence 100: `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` gives the denied checks `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` the same key, so denial of the first forces an incorrect cached denial of the second for 30 seconds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a cache key collision vulnerability. Looking at line 30-31 in the diff: `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. When concatenating strings with underscores as separators, keys like (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") would both produce the same cache key string (e.g., "ns.perm_uid_action_a_b_c"). This is a real collision bug that could cause incorrect denial caching - if one check is denied and cached, a different check with different name/parent values could incorrectly return a cached denial.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — P1, confidence 100: after `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` at line 154 records a denied check, `if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(ctx, permDenialKey); ok { return &authzv1.CheckResponse{Allowed: false}, nil }` returns false for the 30-second TTL without reloading permissions, so a permission grant or folder move immediately after the denial is invisibly rejected even though the positive-cache path falls back to the database when its cached scope does not allow the request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a cache inconsistency issue. Looking at the diff: 1) At line 117-121, if permDenialCache has an entry, it immediately returns Allowed:false without any database check. 2) At line 154, denials are cached with `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)`. 3) The shortCacheTTL is 30 seconds (from line 85 in the setup). 4) The positive permission cache path (lines 123-135) does fall back to database when cached permissions don't allow the request. However, the denial cache path has no such fallback - it returns false immediately. This means if permissions are granted after a denial is cached, the user will be incorrectly denied for up to 30 seconds. This is a real correctness bug where the denial cache is more aggressive than the permission cache, creating an asymmetric caching behavior that can reject valid requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — P3 (confidence 75): `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` concatenates unescaped request-controlled name and parent, so a denied check for `name="foo_bar", parent="baz"` poisons the identical denial key for an allowed `name="foo", parent="bar_baz"` check and forces an authorization denial for 30 seconds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a cache key collision vulnerability. Looking at the diff, `userPermDenialCacheKey` at line 31 concatenates `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` without any escaping or delimiter that prevents collisions. If name="foo_bar" and parent="baz", the key would be identical to name="foo" and parent="bar_baz" (both produce "...foo_bar_baz"). Since this cache stores denial decisions (line 153: `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)`), a denied check could poison the cache for a different resource that should be allowed, causing incorrect authorization denials for the cache TTL (30 seconds based on shortCacheTTL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — [P2, confidence 100] The only denial-cache test injects `s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)` rather than producing a denied `Check`, so deleting the new production write `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` at pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 leaves every test green and the denial cache is never populated.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test coverage gap. Looking at the diff, the test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' at line 973 manually sets `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, userPermDenialCacheKey(...), true)` to test the denial cache read path, but there's no test that verifies the production code at line 154 (`s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)`) actually populates the denial cache when a check is denied. This means the write path of the denial cache is untested - if someone removed line 154, all tests would still pass. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added logic, not a bug in the production code itself.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test coverage gap. Looking at the test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' (lines 959-980), it only tests one specific combination of (user, action, name, parent). The test uses userPermDenialCacheKey with specific values and only checks that one resource is denied. If the cache key function in cache.go:30-31 were modified to remove 'name + "_" + parent', the test would still pass because it only checks one resource. A more robust test would verify that denying dash1/fold1 does NOT deny dash2/fold2, ensuring the cache key properly distinguishes between different resources. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added functionality, not a bug in the production code itself.
